What is happening?

Explain it like I’m five

Each drone is a little runner. A target tells it where to go. A formation gives it a place beside its friends. A play tells the whole team what job to do.

Sensors: the team’s eyes and ears

Radar notices nearby drones, even behind obstacles. Optical needs a clear view. Thermal sees moving drones farther away. Acoustic hears fast drones. RF notices drones whose radio link is working.

These are simplified game rules. A placeable sensor marks drones inside its circle; an onboard sensor helps a squad notice enemies and discover field emitters. Orange drones are detected; purple drones are jammed; grey drones are disabled.

Fields: special patches on the floor

Jamming makes orders hard to hear. EMP freezes movement while its pulse is on. Damage drains health; elimination disables on entry. Repair restores health but does not revive disabled drones. Attract, repel and vortex fields change motion.

Field avoidance is steering, not a force shield. A large, overlapping field or too little room can still catch drones. Adaptive squads give known danger more space, spread out near it and retreat at low health.

Roles: different jobs

Scouts see farther and move quickly. Guards and strikers can tag opponents when combat is enabled. Jammers disrupt nearby opponents. Medics heal nearby teammates. Relays help nearby teammates keep receiving orders in jamming.

Escort follows a friendly squad. Patrol visits your targets. Pincer approaches a detected enemy from two sides. Retreat heads for a repair field, or home. Hold stays near the squad’s spawn point.

Reactions: “if this, do that”

A rule is a tiny promise: when jammed → spread out. Rules run from top to bottom. The first newly true rule wins, and its condition must clear before it can fire again. The cooldown prevents immediate repeats.

Only the health rule uses the health threshold. Reactions take priority over animation cues for their cooldown duration (at least two seconds). Attack orders still require the combat switch to fire tags.

“Adaptive” means predictable situation-based rules here, not a trained AI model. The activity log and squad status tell you why behavior changed.

Animator: a dance with a clock

A cue says “at 0 seconds, make a ring; at 8 seconds, make a wedge.” Play runs the clock. The playhead lets you inspect a moment and pauses the sequence. Drones fly toward the new places instead of teleporting. Rewind starts the sequence again; Reset swarm also revives drones.

Spacing and spin slide between cue values. Role, sensor and reaction rules stay as you set them. Load example replaces the selected squad’s animation only.
